description: Wire fixtures for the sync contract, shared by every lane: the server drives them through HTTP, the device through its fake client, so a drift in the contract is caught here and not when the parts are first put together. Change them only together with libs/protocol/sync.ts.

fixtures.name: cursor-ack
fixtures.description: Acknowledges the highest serverSeq applied across all scopes, and is answered with 204 and no body. there is no backfill endpoint and no backfill response shape — a new scope starts at 0 and is pulled (see pull-new-scope.json).

fixtures.name: hlc-format
fixtures.description: The HLC as it travels: physical unix milliseconds zero-padded to 15 digits, counter to 5, then the device id, which may itself contain colons. The padding is the point — the server compares the column as text, and that order has to be the domain order. Times beside them are UTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds.

fixtures.name: optional-fields
fixtures.description: Every optional and nullable field at its edge, so both sides read them the same way: a pull request without limit, a delete tombstone whose data is null, a row whose nullable fields are all null, an empty text, an empty page with no scopes advanced, and an accepted result with no detail. The enrolment carries every nullable field it has, the student's own archiving stamp included: a clean install has no local row to merge, so a key left off the wire is a key that never arrives.

fixtures.name: pull-new-scope
fixtures.description: A course the student has just been enrolled on. The client has no position for it, the server reports it in scopes, and its history arrives through this ordinary pull. There is no backfill endpoint: this fixture IS the backfill.

fixtures.name: pull-page
fixtures.description: A pull page mixing two scopes: the course content going down and the student own rows. hasMore is true, so cursors carry the position each scope reached.

fixtures.name: pull-school-scope
fixtures.description: A student who holds a role in a school but is enrolled on nothing. The school scope carries the school itself, its courses and the groups of those courses; no lesson, version or section rides it, because content belongs to the course scope and the student has no course scope at all. The groups are what a student who is not enrolled reads before asking for a place, which is why they ride the school and not the course: the course scope is exactly what they do not have. Both statuses travel — recruitment is closed by the status, and a group whose recruitment has closed still has to reach the device, or it stays in the catalogue for ever.

fixtures.name: push-mixed
fixtures.description: A batch whose rows are answered one by one: results has the length of changes and the same order, and a refusal leaves its neighbours applied.

fixtures.name: push-natural-key
fixtures.description: The second device of one student hands in a section the first has already handed in, under a local id of its own. The table's key is the natural one (enrolment, version, section), so the server writes onto the row that key already holds and the HLC decides the text. The answer names both ids: docId is what was sent, serverDocId is the row it landed in. Without the second the device would keep a local row the server has never heard of — carried by no pull, removed by no tombstone — beside the winning row arriving as a second answer to one section.

fixtures.name: push-rejections
fixtures.description: Every rejection reason, once each. The work stays on the device in all seven cases: a refusal is a state of the row, never a lost edit.

fixtures.name: push-restamped
fixtures.description: serverHlc comes back on every accepted row, not only when it differs. Here the first row is a genuine repeat (same stamp, same body) and keeps its HLC; the second arrived from a device whose clock is a year fast, or whose id is shared with another phone restored from the same backup, and the server restamped it. Both records are kept; neither write is swallowed as an imagined repeat.

fixtures.name: request-errors
fixtures.description: The failures that are not per-row. Too many scopes is refused with a code rather than answered with a silently truncated list.
